i.norm: Tests DefaultParser behaviour when encountering unrecognized options. Covers the IGNORE action (silently skip unknown flags) and the THROW action (raise UnrecognizedOptionException for unknown flags).
Define three individual options that may or may not be included in an option set.
baseOptions recognises only -a and -b; -c and -d are both unrecognized here.
specificOptions recognises -a, -b, and -c; only -d is unrecognized.
Input contains two known flags (-a, -b), one conditionally known flag (-c), one completely unknown flag (-d), and two plain positional arguments.

--- Scenario 1: IGNORE unknown options --- With IGNORE, unrecognized flags (-c, -d) are silently dropped. Only -a and -b are recognised by baseOptions, so 2 options should be parsed. The two plain arguments (arg1, arg2) are retained as leftover args.
--- Scenario 2: THROW on unknown options --- With THROW, encountering -d (unrecognized by specificOptions) must throw. The exception message must identify the offending flag.
